hook_text: Same city, two photos from the same plane. One looks like a map. One looks like a postcard. Why?
clip_script: Tilt the camera and you get an oblique photograph. You see the sides of the hotels, the harbour, maybe the horizon. Easy to recognise. But things far away shrink, so you cannot measure with it. Point the camera straight down and you get a vertical photograph. Just roofs, roads, treetops. It looks like a map without labels. Harder to read, but the scale stays almost the same, so you can measure. How do you read it? Clues. Straight lines and neat shapes: people made it. Curves and ragged edges: nature made it. Long shadows: something tall. Dark and smooth: probably water. And the scale? Lens length divided by flying height.
visual_style: A whiteboard aircraft with two camera beams, one angled and one straight down, producing a postcard-style sketch and a map-like sketch of the same coastline.
pacing: Quick contrast, then a steady run through the clues.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to learn how to calculate photo scale.
